issues.label: Appealability of stay order
issues.why: The court must determine whether the stay order is directly appealable or reviewable only by writ.

issues.label: Proper standard of review
issues.why: The court must select de novo versus abuse-of-discretion review for interpreting the bylaw clause and granting a stay.

issues.label: Court power to stay action
issues.why: The court must identify the statutory/inherent authority for staying a California action based on another forum or contract.

issues.label: Bylaw is binding contract
issues.why: The court must decide whether corporate bylaws constitute an enforceable contract against a shareholder like Salamon.

issues.label: Salamon assent to bylaws
issues.why: The court must decide if and how a shareholder is deemed to have notice/assented to bylaw amendments or existing bylaws.

issues.label: Valid adoption of forum bylaw
issues.why: The court must confirm the bylaw was properly adopted under Delaware corporate law and corporate governance procedures.

issues.label: Bylaw interpretation law
issues.why: The court must decide whether Delaware or California law governs interpretation of a Delaware corporation’s bylaws.

issues.label: Choice-of-law default rules
issues.why: Because there is no bylaw choice-of-law clause, the court must apply conflicts principles to select governing law.

issues.label: Internal affairs doctrine scope
issues.why: The court must decide whether shareholder inspection rights are an internal corporate affair for a Delaware corporation.

issues.label: Inspection as internal affairs under CA
issues.why: The court must determine California’s view on whether inspection of a foreign corporation implicates internal affairs.

issues.label: Inspection as internal affairs under DE
issues.why: The court must determine Delaware’s classification of inspection demands and related governance disputes.

issues.label: Clause covers this “action”
issues.why: The court must decide whether a petition to compel inspection is an “action asserting a claim… governed by the internal affairs doctrine.”

issues.label: Mandatory vs permissive clause
issues.why: The court must confirm the clause is exclusive/mandatory and not merely a consent-to-jurisdiction provision.

issues.label: Triggering language satisfied
issues.why: The court must decide whether Salamon’s statutory inspection petition is a “claim against the corporation” within the clause.

issues.label: Non-signatory enforcement
issues.why: The court must decide whether the corporation may enforce the clause against a shareholder who did not sign it.

issues.label: Equitable enforcement doctrines
issues.why: The court must consider doctrines like direct-benefits estoppel or corporate contract principles supporting enforcement.

issues.label: Unconscionability analysis
issues.why: The court must consider procedural/substantive unconscionability or unfairness as a defense to enforcing the clause.

issues.label: Fraud/overreaching defense
issues.why: The court must assess whether the clause resulted from fraud, coercion, or inequitable conduct.

issues.label: Reasonableness of chosen forum
issues.why: The court must consider whether Delaware Chancery is a reasonable forum given parties, witnesses, and subject matter.

issues.label: Public policy exception
issues.why: The court must decide whether enforcing the clause contravenes a fundamental California public policy.

issues.label: Unwaivable CA inspection rights
issues.why: The court must determine whether Corp. Code §§1600/1601 create nonwaivable rights that override private forum selection.

issues.label: Section 1600 absolute list right
issues.why: The court must decide whether §1600’s “absolute right” to the shareholder list can be displaced by Delaware forum selection.

issues.label: Section 1601 proper-purpose right
issues.why: The court must decide whether §1601’s inspection right for domestic corporations applies to this foreign corporation and, if so, how.

issues.label: Foreign corporation coverage
issues.why: The court must decide whether and to what extent §§1600/1601 apply to Delaware corporations doing business in California.

issues.label: Pseudo-foreign corporation statutes
issues.why: The court must consider whether California pseudo-foreign corporation provisions (e.g., Corp. Code §2115) affect governance/inspection.

issues.label: Commerce/constitutional limits
issues.why: The court must consider constitutional limits on applying California corporate governance statutes to Delaware corporations.

issues.label: VantagePoint/DE primacy
issues.why: The court must consider Delaware and California precedents limiting California’s reach over internal affairs of Delaware corporations.

issues.label: DGCL §220 adequacy
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether Delaware’s §220 provides an adequate substitute remedy for California inspection rights.

issues.label: Comparative breadth of rights
issues.why: The court must decide whether differences in scope (records, time period, tax returns, audits) make Delaware remedy materially inadequate.

issues.label: Burden of proof on policy
issues.why: The court must allocate who bears the burden to show enforcement violates public policy or is unreasonable.

issues.label: Proper purpose under §220
issues.why: If Delaware law controls, the court must assess whether Salamon’s stated purposes qualify as “proper” and whether mixed motives matter.

issues.label: Improper purpose/extortion allegation
issues.why: The court must decide how allegations of extortion/harassment affect enforceability of inspection demands or forum selection.

issues.label: Scope of inspection requested
issues.why: The court must determine whether each category requested is within the statutory/contractual inspection rights and necessary to stated purposes.

issues.label: Shareholder-list inspection scope
issues.why: The court must decide whether Salamon is entitled to names/addresses/shareholdings and under what conditions (time, form, copying).

issues.label: Financial statements and audits
issues.why: The court must determine whether quarterly/annual statements and independent audits are inspectable under the governing statute.

issues.label: Tax returns inspectability
issues.why: The court must decide whether corporate tax returns are subject to inspection and what privacy/confidentiality protections apply.

issues.label: Minutes and committee records
issues.why: The court must decide whether board/shareholder minutes and committee materials are within inspection rights and any limitations.

issues.label: Loans and off-balance obligations
issues.why: The court must decide whether records about loans to directors/off-balance-sheet loans are inspectable as related to valuation or mismanagement.

issues.label: Token treasury accounting records
issues.why: The court must decide whether records about OXT holdings/treasury are corporate “books and records” subject to inspection.

issues.label: Gambling-law complaints records
issues.why: The court must decide whether documents/communications about alleged gambling violations are inspectable for mismanagement investigation.

issues.label: Attorney-client privilege limits
issues.why: The court must consider privilege as a limitation on inspection (especially board communications re legal compliance).

issues.label: Work-product doctrine limits
issues.why: The court must consider whether litigation/investigation materials are protected from inspection.

issues.label: Trade secret/confidential info
issues.why: The court must consider protective orders or confidentiality conditions for sensitive business and technical records.

issues.label: Confidentiality undertakings
issues.why: The court must decide whether to condition inspection on NDAs or use restrictions, and whether such conditions are permissible.

issues.label: Timing and manner of inspection
issues.why: The court must determine where, when, and how inspection occurs (principal office in CA vs Delaware) under the governing regime.

issues.label: Contractor status relevance
issues.why: The court must consider whether Salamon’s former contractor relationship affects purpose, access, or defenses (e.g., misuse of info).

issues.label: Standing as shareholder
issues.why: The court must confirm Salamon’s shareholder status, percentage ownership, and record-holder/beneficial-holder status for statutory standing.

issues.label: Ownership threshold under §1600
issues.why: The court must determine whether Salamon meets the 5% threshold for §1600’s shareholder list right.

issues.label: Demand sufficiency
issues.why: The court must decide whether Salamon’s written demand met statutory formalities (content, verification, specificity) under the applicable law.

issues.label: Improper denial consequences
issues.why: The court must consider statutory remedies, penalties, or fee-shifting for wrongful refusal if California law applies.

issues.label: Remedy type: mandate
issues.why: The court must decide whether writ of mandate is the proper procedural vehicle for enforcing inspection rights in California.

issues.label: Forum clause vs mandate remedy
issues.why: The court must decide whether an exclusive-forum bylaw can require dismissal/stay of a mandamus proceeding.

issues.label: Stay vs dismissal choice
issues.why: The court must decide whether the proper enforcement of the clause is a stay, dismissal, or transfer-like relief.

issues.label: First-to-file doctrine
issues.why: The court must consider whether California or Delaware filing sequence affects comity, stay, or discretionary abstention.

issues.label: Comity and parallel proceedings
issues.why: The court must consider comity principles governing whether to defer to a sister-state proceeding involving overlapping issues.

issues.label: Effect of Delaware dismissal
issues.why: The court must determine how Delaware Chancery’s dismissal for lack of personal jurisdiction affects the basis for a stay.

issues.label: Availability of Delaware forum
issues.why: The court must decide whether the clause is enforceable when Delaware cannot exercise personal jurisdiction over Salamon in the filed action.

issues.label: Forum non conveniens principles
issues.why: The court must consider whether to apply forum non conveniens standards when enforcing an exclusive-forum bylaw.

issues.label: Anti-suit and equitable concerns
issues.why: The court must consider whether the Delaware declaratory action was anticipatory or tactical and how that affects equitable enforcement.

issues.label: Issue preclusion from Delaware
issues.why: The court must consider whether any Delaware rulings (e.g., personal jurisdiction) have collateral-estoppel or res judicata effects.

issues.label: Judicial notice propriety
issues.why: The court must confirm what Delaware filings/orders may be judicially noticed and for what purposes.

issues.label: Burden on movant for stay
issues.why: The court must decide what Orchid must show to obtain a stay based on a forum clause and parallel litigation.

issues.label: Prejudice from delay
issues.why: The court must weigh prejudice to Salamon from being stayed (valuation, communication with shareholders, potential wrongdoing ongoing).

issues.label: Risk of inconsistent rulings
issues.why: The court must consider whether proceeding in California risks conflicting determinations with Delaware on governing law and inspection scope.

issues.label: Internal affairs vs local interests
issues.why: The court must balance Delaware’s interest in uniform corporate governance against California’s interest in protecting resident shareholders.

issues.label: Interpretation of “employee” term
issues.why: The court must consider whether the clause’s reference to claims against employees affects coverage if relief requires actions by officers/employees.

issues.label: Subsidiary records inclusion
issues.why: The court must decide whether inspection rights extend to records of Orchid Labs, Inc. as a subsidiary and under what conditions.

issues.label: Principal place of business factor
issues.why: The court must consider whether being headquartered in California affects applicability of California inspection statutes or policy.

issues.label: Statutory construction of §1601
issues.why: The court must interpret “domestic corporation” and “principal office in California” language to see if it reaches Orchid.

issues.label: Statutory construction of §1600
issues.why: The court must interpret whether §1600’s shareholder-list right applies to foreign corporations or only California corporations.

issues.label: Federal preemption/crypto regulation
issues.why: The court must consider whether any federal regulatory regime over tokens/financial records impacts disclosure obligations or confidentiality.

issues.label: Protective order for compliance materials
issues.why: The court must consider limiting disclosure of sensitive compliance/legal-risk materials while preserving any inspection entitlement.

issues.label: Attorney fees and costs
issues.why: The court must consider whether any fee-shifting applies under the governing inspection statute or equitable principles.

issues.label: Mootness
issues.why: The court must consider whether the dispute is moot if circumstances change (e.g., records provided or shares sold).

issues.label: Ripeness and justiciability
issues.why: The court must confirm an actual controversy exists regarding inspection and that the requested relief is presently needed.

issues.label: Scope of stay order
issues.why: The court must define whether the stay halts all proceedings or allows limited discovery/briefing on threshold issues like enforceability.

issues.label: Security/bond considerations
issues.why: The court must consider whether to require conditions to mitigate harm from a stay (e.g., expedited Delaware §220 demand process).

issues.label: Abuse of discretion factors
issues.why: If discretionary, the court must articulate and apply proper factors guiding a stay decision to avoid arbitrary enforcement.
